The Assyrian royal corpus is partisan and its parallel witnesses are one lineage.
The Hebrew textual path requires composition, textual-layer and dependency review before it can count independently.
The held-out primary candidate’s exact 701 coverage and expression count remain sealed and may be inconclusive.
Automated repository checks cannot prove a person’s complete browsing history.

decision_scope: Proceed to strict preregistration and post-freeze non-map evidence collection. Reconstruction, spatial inputs and polygon generation remain blocked.
frozen_question: During the 701 BCE horizon of Sennacherib’s third campaign and its directly reported political dispositions, which named localities in the Joppa–Ekron–Lachish–Jerusalem corridor can non-territorial-map evidence support as local-control points, transfer objects, contested places or unresolved localities of Judah, Ekron, Ashdod, Gaza and Ashkelon while keeping conquest, tribute, suzerainty, military presence and local administration distinct?
go_rationale: The question, campaign horizon and corridor are bounded without false precision.
Five candidate political entities have explicit textual paths.
Twelve named spatial candidates and more than four potential source lineages make a disciplined post-freeze evidence round feasible.
Conflicts and exclusions are already visible, so the protocol can fail honestly without manufacturing a polygon.
A metadata-only comparator and twenty fixed evaluation units make a later held-out test structurally possible.

go_thresholds.basis: The era/year contract records year_bce=701, campaign_horizon resolution and chronology uncertainty.
go_thresholds.criterion: A 701 BCE campaign/disposition horizon can be defined without claiming a day-level snapshot.

go_thresholds.basis: Judah/Hezekiah, Ekron/Padî, Ashdod/Mitinti, Gaza/Ṣilli-Bēl and Ashkelon/Ṣidqâ are named.
go_thresholds.criterion: At least four political entities have textual paths.

go_thresholds.basis: Ashkelon has four named cities of Ṣidqâ plus its royal seat; Judah has Jerusalem and a Lachish path, with the latter still source-critical and not yet admitted as local control.
go_thresholds.criterion: At least two entities each have two potential named-locality relations.

go_thresholds.basis: Twelve named candidates are locked; exact reviewed coordinates remain a post-freeze gap.
go_thresholds.criterion: At least ten locatable spatial candidates exist.

go_thresholds.basis: Assyrian royal inscriptions, Lachish excavation, southwest-Judah archaeological critique, the local Ekron excavation/inscription tradition and the Deuteronomistic textual tradition are distinct candidate lineages; independence of claims still requires review.
go_thresholds.criterion: At least four potentially independent source lineages exist.

go_thresholds.basis: Regional destruction dates may predate 701; unnamed transfers cannot be geolocated; imperial relations cannot be equated with local administration; Bible-text independence remains unresolved.
go_thresholds.criterion: At least two counterevidence, conflict or exclusion paths exist.

go_thresholds.basis: ORACC Q identifiers and lines, DOI-addressed IAA/BASOR records, a Harvard publication record and verse locators are recorded with rights scopes.
go_thresholds.criterion: Principal material has legal access and stable locators.

go_thresholds.basis: The registered comprehensive Carta atlas is plausibly capable of expressing eight or more of twenty fixed units; exact expression remains sealed and can yield an inconclusive result.
go_thresholds.criterion: A metadata-only held-out comparator could express at least eight locked units.

held_out_finding: One atlas is registered from bibliographic metadata only. The Oxford Bible Atlas was excluded after a search result exposed a front-cover thumbnail. Unrelated results for The Bible Atlas exposed map-label and route summaries; that work was excluded without opening any linked PDF.

map_body_audit.audit_note: No map body or derivative was selected for inspection. Search-result thumbnail/label leakage is disclosed and the affected publications are excluded.

ontology_finding: The audit records local dynastic rule, contested local authority, territorial transfer, imperial suzerainty, tribute obligation, military presence, siege/conquest, destruction event and local administration as separate layers. Only the last can directly authorize a local-control point.

source_access_finding: Six preliminary research sources are admitted with citation, locator, rights and lineage metadata. Indexed ORACC text provides stable Q identifiers and lines despite page-fetch failures; full-text follow-up remains an evidence-round task.
source_lineage_finding: ORACC Q003496 and Q003945 are parallel witnesses within one Assyrian royal-inscription tradition. Different copies and modern translations do not increase the independent-lineage count automatically. Archaeological, local inscriptional and biblical textual paths require their own dependency review.
temporal_finding: The scope is the conventionally dated 701 BCE campaign and directly reported disposition horizon. It is year/horizon-resolved, not day-resolved. Astronomical year −700 is a computational conversion only and is never stored as a negative ISO date.
